parameters.content:
## What this is for

api.weather.gov is the surface 50 of 54 AD4 markets actually SETTLE on. The
repo previously tried to reach it by scraping an HTML page; that parser was
never finished, so every live reading silently fell through to IEM.

This workflow reads the documented JSON instead, and it costs nothing: the
API imposes no rate limit based on User-Agent. That is also why the IEM 429
that kept killing the Live Weather Monitor stops mattering for US cities.

Three calls per city, all keyed on data `cities` already holds:

  /stations/{icao}/observations/latest   the reading, with QC flags and a
                                         station-reported 24h maximum
  /alerts/active?point={lat},{lon}       heat advisories and warnings
  /points/{lat},{lon}                    today's SOLAR TRANSIT - the sun's
                                         zenith, which is the physical anchor
                                         of the daily temperature peak

Non-US cities 404 and are skipped. They keep using IEM.

## Where it writes, and why nothing new was needed

  weather_observations   source='NWS', beside the existing source='IEM' rows.
                         The unique key is (city_key, valid_at, source), so
                         both feeds coexist per timestamp - which is what
                         makes them COMPARABLE. That comparison is the
                         evidence the settlement gate has been waiting for.

  live_weather           one row per city: the running max, the trend, and now
                         solar_transit_at, max_temp_24h_c and the active NWS
                         alert.

  weather_events         kind='nws_alert' / 'temp_spike'. P1.1 already emails
                         unnotified events and they are on the Realtime
                         publication, so alerts reach you and the UI feed with
                         NO new plumbing.

An alert only raises an event when it CHANGES. Re-running this workflow ten
times does not send ten emails.

assignments.name: alert_events
assignments.value: Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, Extreme Heat Warning, Extreme Heat Watch, Excessive Heat Watch

nodes.name: Save NWS ids
nodes.notes: PATCH, not upsert. An upsert here fails with 23502 on any database whose cities.display_name is NOT NULL, because ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE checks NOT NULL on the proposed row before it finds the conflict - and it fails with PGRST102 whenever one run has both a supported and an unsupported city, because a bulk POST needs identical keys. This workflow annotates a city that already exists; it must never create one.
